edges.description: CCBE1 is the cofactor that lets ADAMTS3 cleave pro-VEGF-C into its mature active form; without it, that cleavage step fails.
Without mature VEGF-C, VEGFR-3 signaling in lymphatic endothelial cells is not driven and lymphatic vessels fail to form.
Defective lymphangiogenesis produces malformed, dysfunctional lymphatic vessels throughout the body.
Dysplastic intestinal lymphatics dilate and leak lymph into the gut lumen.
Impaired lymphatic drainage in the limbs, genitalia, and face causes lymphedema.
Enteric loss of lymph depletes serum albumin and immunoglobulins.
Enteric protein loss lowers serum albumin.
Enteric loss of lymph depletes serum immunoglobulins.
Enteric loss of lymph depletes circulating lymphocytes.
Loss of Ccbe1 in the mouse blocks budding and migration of Prox1-positive lymphatic endothelial cells from the cardinal vein, which is exactly the cellular step this node names.
edges.limitations: The model speaks to the cellular step, not to the upstream activation node: VEGFR-3 activation appeared unaltered in the mutants by proximity ligation assay, so this animal does not itself demonstrate reduced receptor signalling and is not linked to the proteolytic-activation node. Being a constitutive null, it also models complete loss rather than the hypomorphic alleles many patients carry.

edges.description: Complete absence of definitive lymphatics models the severe end of the human generalized lymphatic dysplasia, and is consistent with the recurrent hydrops fetalis seen in some HKLLS1 pregnancies.
edges.limitations: Ccbe1-null mice die prenatally, so the model cannot express the postnatal arms of the human disease - chronic limb, genital and facial lymphedema, intestinal lymphangiectasia with protein-losing enteropathy, or the craniofacial and cognitive features. Human patients carry hypomorphic as well as null alleles and survive, so the null mouse is more severe than the usual human phenotype.

edges.description: ccbe1 mutants fail lymphangioblast budding and venous sprouting, and ccbe1 acts at the same developmental stage as vegfc, which is the cellular lymphangiogenic step this node names.
edges.limitations: Zebrafish do not develop the craniofacial, cognitive, intestinal or chronic lymphedema features of the human syndrome, so the model speaks to the developmental lymphangiogenic step and not to the downstream clinical phenotype.

edges.description: Maps loss of CCBE1 function onto specific protein domains, and shows that a Hennekam syndrome mutation in the collagen repeats is more damaging than one in an EGF domain - a structural account of why HKLLS1 alleles differ in severity.
edges.limitations: The severity ordering was established for two patient mutations, so it supports a domain-level rule rather than a validated genotype-phenotype predictor for individual HKLLS1 alleles. The knock-ins delete whole domains, which is a more drastic lesion than most patient missense variants.

edges.description: The same allelic series was read out directly on VEGF-C processing, so it assays the proteolytic activation step itself rather than only its downstream consequence. Collagen-domain deletion abolishes processing while EGF-domain deletion does not, which assigns the cleavage-supporting function of CCBE1 to the collagen repeats.
edges.limitations: The processing readout is an in vitro assay on deletion constructs, not a measurement of endogenous VEGF-C maturation in a patient or in the knock-in animal. It establishes which domain carries the activity rather than quantifying how much activation a given patient allele retains.

The same asymmetry holds for two Hennekam syndrome patient mutations, one in each domain, which is what makes this an allele-specific model of the human disorder rather than a generic knockout.

nodes.description: The hypogammaglobulinemia of HKLLS1 is a secondary immunodeficiency driven by enteric loss of immunoglobulin, not a primary defect of B-cell development, so the dietary control of lymph loss is the treatment that addresses the cause. Immunoglobulin replacement is used for symptomatic hypogammaglobulinemia alongside it; intravenous administration does not always achieve satisfactory plasma levels, and subcutaneous administration has been reported to do better in intestinal lymphangiectasia. Two genotype-confirmed CCBE1 patients in one kindred document its use in HKLLS1 itself, one of whom no longer needed replacement once the medium-chain-triglyceride diet was optimized.

nodes.description: CCBE1 and the protease ADAMTS3 form a complex that cleaves the poorly active 29/31-kDa form of pro-VEGF-C into the mature 21/23-kDa ligand. Loss of CCBE1 removes the cofactor, so this proteolytic maturation step fails and little active VEGF-C is produced. CCBE1's two domains contribute differently: the C-terminal collagen-like domain drives the cleavage activity, while the N-terminal EGF-like domain colocalizes pro-VEGF-C with its protease at the lymphatic endothelial cell surface.

nodes.description: Recurrent homozygous missense CCBE1 allele, reported in two Turkish siblings of consanguineous parents and previously in a Dutch kindred. It is one of a cluster of alleles hitting cysteine residues in the EGF domain, whose disulfide linkages make them likely to disrupt the domain's tertiary structure. Functionally it is notable for a split result: in transfected cells the mutant protein shows increased intracellular expression and increased secretion, yet CCBE1 is scarce in the patients' own intestinal tissue by immunohistochemistry. The authors leave the reconciliation open between a secreted-but-misfolded protein and one that is rapidly degraded in vivo, so this allele is not loss-of-expression at the synthesis level without being a protein that is present where it is needed.
